Native launcher verification

Verify native ownership through the real desktop wrapper and the app launcher.

About 3 min read · 3 sections

On this page
01 Isolated regression 02 Startup diagnostics 03 Installed startup and restart

The ChatGPT app's codex-cli/bin/codex is a shell launcher, not a symlink. Shared-native verification resolves it to the signed CodexCLI.app engine, while an existing host's base receipt can still name the launcher. Test both spellings against the verified native engine and retain the receipt's recorded checksum. A test that starts every process with the signed binary misses this boundary.

Isolated regression

Run scripts/e2e-shared-native.mjs against a complete candidate package, with its verified gateway SDK available. Alongside the usual --gateway, --package, --root, --candidate-engine, and --host-capabilities native,gateway, pass:

--desktop-app /Applications/ChatGPT.app
--adapter-codex /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex
--host-codex /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex

Keep --codex on the app's signed executable. --candidate-engine must match that executable's exact version. This mode starts the real host with the launcher, uses a normally generated desktop wrapper for stdio, and passes the launcher through the Unix adapter. The host uses production native SDK verification. Also run without --host-codex to cover hosts that already record the signed path.

The fixture uses fresh private homes and mock providers. It never copies native authentication or edits the primary native configuration. Its output records which path variants were used, whether an ownership mismatch occurred, and whether all owned processes were cleaned up.

Startup diagnostics

Recent ChatGPT builds call app-server --print-startup-config before they open their normal RPC session. The registered wrapper recognizes app-server help and version requests, the --print-* diagnostic family, and every app-server subcommand expressed as an unconsumed positional token. Those invocations go straight to the original CLI with their argv, standard streams, environment, and exit status unchanged; they do not read gateway configuration, state, credentials, catalog, relay, or start an adapter.

The boundary is deliberately narrow. An unknown app-server option, a value after an option that takes one (including -c/--config), and arguments after -- remain normal adapter sessions. A positional token that has not been consumed by one of those options is the original CLI's subcommand, including hidden, future, and invalid commands. This prevents future session flags or literal configuration text from silently changing providers while leaving CLI command ownership with the native engine. --print-* is the reserved diagnostic namespace, so future startup probes do not need another wrapper change.

Installed startup and restart

scripts/probe-desktop-wrapper.mjs performs read-only startup checks through the exact registered wrapper. Pass --wrapper /absolute/registered-wrapper, --native-home /absolute/native-home, and --output /tmp/startup-result.json. It initializes a client, reads organization requirements, lists models, and lists one page of chats. It records success, counts, and numeric error codes, without chat contents, configuration values, or inference.

Require those checks before and after the normal service restart, confirm desktop registration remains active for future launches, and require gateway rollout --verify --json to report ready on each machine. A temporary CODEX_CLI_PATH override, a passing direct-binary fixture, or an opened app alone is insufficient. Service restarts must retain their normal idle guard; a refused restart is pending verification and does not authorize stopping active work.
